A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UAE-3D/UDM-3D. All 13 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v3, including appendices, are readable. Text, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular reconstruction, unconditional and conditional generation, timing, and DiT-ablation results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds augmentation, latent-dimensionality, loss-weight, reconstruction and molecular-structure analyses.

M1.justification: v3 revises the stated distance-reconstruction loss: v1 Equation 19 weights atom pairs uniformly, whereas v3 Equations 10–11 assign bonded pairs weight 1+lambda. This modifies one existing objective component; the encoder, decoder, DiT, augmentation strategy and CFG procedure remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use QM9 and GEOM-Drugs for molecular modeling and retain conditioning on the same six QM9 properties. Added diagnostics concern these datasets and already-used geometric transformations. Protein, RNA and text-guided generation remain proposed future work.

E2.justification: v3 adds EQGAT-diff to both datasets' generation comparisons, ADiT to QM9 generation and reconstruction comparisons, and GeoBFN to conditional generation (Tables 1–3 and 9). These are evaluated additions, including a directly relevant unified-latent competitor; the corresponding existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds molecule-stability metrics, ring-distribution evaluation, controlled augmentation comparisons, and explicit latent-dimension and loss-weight sweeps. Its appendix also reports a QM9 split of 100K/10K/10K, conflicting with the 100K/18K/13K split retained from v1 in Section 4.1. The added evaluation designs are clear, but the split discrepancy does not establish which split was actually used.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's DiT-versus-Transformer ablation, v3 tests rotation/translation augmentation effects on generation and reconstruction, latent dimensionality, and bonded-distance weighting (Tables 5–8). It also adds geometric latent-trajectory visualizations, ring-distribution analysis and generated-molecule case studies (Figures 4–8 and Table 10).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The expanded results continue to use point estimates.

E6.justification: Reported UDM-3D values change: QM9 FCD 0.161 to 0.130, GEOM-Drugs V&U&N 0.958 to 0.907, and conditional polarizability MAE 1.76 to 1.54 (v1 Tables 2–4; v3 Tables 1–3). v3 also adds substantial comparator, stability, reconstruction and diagnostic results. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting gains, given the revised objective and unresolved split documentation.

T1.justification: The reconstruction-distance definition is substantively revised through the bond-dependent weighting in v3 Equations 10–11. The remaining VAE, diffusion and CFG mathematics is largely equivalent after consolidation and renumbering; neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of unified near-lossless compression, generic DiT generation and improved quality/efficiency remain. v3 adds structured geometric variation of learned latents to the introduction's claimed findings. Its new quantitative GEOM-Drugs abstract highlights largely summarize results already reported in v1.

C2.justification: v3 adds a concrete limitation concerning molecule sizes sampled from the training distribution and explicitly discusses applicability boundaries (Appendix A). It adds interpretations of geometric latent trajectories, dimensionality and loss-weight tradeoffs, and ADiT's poor reported scores in relation to evaluation protocols (Section 4.5 and Appendices B–D).

D1.justification: Where v1 largely directs readers to code for hyperparameters, v3 Table 11 documents epochs, optimizer, learning rate, architecture sizes, latent dimension, loss weights and condition dropout. Appendices A and D disclose size sampling, conformer selection, coordinate centering and the reused EDM property predictor. These are principally new disclosures. However, v3 omits v1's explicit anonymous code-access link.

R1.justification: Appendix C substantially expands positioning against concurrent ADiT and MolCRAFT, discussing compression fidelity, bond information, evaluation and task scope. Additional positioning covers GeoBFN, hierarchical latent diffusion, masked graph modeling and molecule-language research. The earlier molecular-VAE discussion is retained in the appendix rather than removed.

P1.justification: v3 condenses and reworks the background and methodology exposition, flattens subsection structure, revises the results narrative, and reorganizes supplementary material into Appendices A–D. Existing molecular-VAE discussion and algorithms move within this structure. The title, author list and citation style also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v1's reconstruction table and timing figure become the combined four-panel Figure 2; the model overview is redrawn. Benchmark tables gain stability columns and highlighted relative differences, the DiT table is transposed, and numerous analysis tables, latent-space plots and molecule visualizations are added.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for design choices that v1 assessed mainly through benchmark scores and a DiT ablation: Tables 5–8 directly examine augmentation, latent capacity and loss weighting, while Table 11 makes training specifications substantially more self-contained. Closer-method comparisons and a concrete size-sampling limitation improve assessment of novelty and scope. These gains outweigh the omitted code link and unresolved reporting problems, particularly conflicting QM9 splits and the unexplained tenfold RMSD difference between Table 6 and Tables 8–9.
